ev.q: Among the 458 participants who reported no recent iron tablet supplementation, 111 (24%) (95% CI=20%--28%) were anemic.
Boys were twice as likely as girls to have low BMI (48% versus 24%; p<0.01)
Among the 190 participants assessed, 49 (26%) (95% CI=23%--30%) had retinol levels that suggested low vitamin A status.
49 (37%) of 134 girls who reported having experienced menarche had anemia compared with 17 (17%) of 99 who had not (p=0.001)
participants aged 10--14 years were 1.7 times as likely to have low BMI as those aged 15--19 years
Participants aged 10--19 years were chosen by systematic random sampling from camp registration data of 26,235 adolescents

methods_quotes.q: Low BMI was determined by comparing a person's BMI to that of persons of similar age and same sex
Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests were used to compare data.
For point estimates of prevalence rates, 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated by the quadratic method.
Data were analyzed using EpiInfo version 6.04b.
